vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: boot-resume
Version: 1.0.0

The 'boot-resume' skill is a utility designed to automatically recover interrupted agent sessions after a gateway crash or restart. It functions by deploying a shell script (boot-resume-check.sh) and a systemd drop-in that triggers the script on service start. The script scans local session JSONL files to detect unfinished tasks and uses the 'openclaw cron' command to inject a resumption prompt. All actions are consistent with the stated purpose of operational resilience, and no indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized remote execution were found.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose (detect interrupted sessions and auto-inject resumes) is plausible and the code stays local, but there are internal inconsistencies and missing files that don't add up and warrant review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims multi-agent support and scans all agent directories, which is consistent with its purpose, but the resume command always uses "--session main" (hard-coded) while the detector explicitly skips session keys that end with ":main". This mismatch suggests the resume jobs may be targeted incorrectly (wrong agent or session namespace). Additionally, install.sh references a templates/boot-resume.conf file, but that file is not listed in the package manifest — a missing artifact that breaks the advertised systemd drop-in deployment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script operate only on local OpenClaw state (sessions.json, session JSONL files, restart-resume.json) and schedule local openclaw cron jobs; there are no external network endpoints or credential usage. This is within the claimed scope. Note: the script will automatically schedule resume events that cause the agent to continue conversations without explicit per-resume user approval — this is the intended behavior but has operational implications.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is local (install.sh copies the script into the user's ~/.openclaw workspace and writes a user-level systemd drop-in). No remote downloads or package installs. However, install.sh copies a template from templates/boot-resume.conf which isn't present in the manifest — the installer would fail or be incomplete unless that file exists elsewhere.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested binaries (python3 and openclaw) and optional OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR are appropriate and proportional to the stated task of parsing session files and invoking openclaw cron. The script only reads OpenClaw state and writes a user-level systemd drop-in and logs to /tmp/openclaw. No unexpected credentials or unrelated env vars are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill installs a user-level systemd drop-in to run on gateway start so it can act automatically after restarts. always:false (not force-included) and user-invocable:true. Autonomous resume of interrupted sessions is the feature, but it increases blast radius (the gateway will schedule actions without manual confirmation). This is expected functionality but important for users to accept consciously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, review and test the script in a safe environment: 1) Inspect scripts/boot-resume-check.sh to confirm resume target is correct for your deployment — note the cron add uses "--session main" while the scanner claims multi-agent support (this mismatch may resume the wrong session/agent). 2) Ensure the systemd drop-in template (templates/boot-resume.conf) exists and is what you expect; the manifest here does not include it. 3) Understand this will schedule automatic resume events that cause agents to continue conversations autonomously — if you don't want automatic actions, do not install the systemd drop-in and run manually with --no-wait. 4) Backup ~/.openclaw/workspace/state/restart-resume.json and test on a non-production instance to observe behavior. If you are not comfortable with automatic resume or with the script targeting, request a corrected build that explicitly maps agent directories to the --session/--session-key parameters and includes the missing template.
